backbone: Transport each specialized Hodge class through Hodge-type integral models to a pullback of a CM class, then reduce CM classes to balanced Weil classes whose divisor pairings are rational.
quote: Our proof also expresses each specialized Hodge class as the pullback, along a rational homomorphism of special fibers, of a specialized Hodge class from a CM abelian variety.

backbone: Assume primes eventually equal A+B; residue restrictions, an amplified moment with Poisson summation and the quadratic large sieve force character biases contradicting a collision estimate.
quote: Our proof uses the simultaneous residue restrictions and coverage of every sufficiently large prime to reach a contradiction without such a classification.

backbone: Greedy steps reduce to A/C; an auxiliary integer M with randomly chosen divisors yields a dense family of short expansions by descent through O(log S) numerator ranges.
quote: The dense family is obtained by descending through $O(\log S)$ numerator ranges.

backbone: Induction on dimension from known low-dimensional and fourfold cases: stable degeneration to a K-polystable cone, stabilizer and jet-cone estimates force smooth Gorenstein cone, then quadric characterization.
quote: Starting from the known cases in dimensions two and three and the fourfold companion, we argue by induction.

backbone: Explicitly build a rank-two bundle G glued along three graphs; quotient sequences prove ampleness, while a Griffiths-positive metric would yield a quadratic limit and incompatible invariant measures.
quote: We construct $G$ together with two line-bundle quotients. Their dual inclusions will span away from three graphs and agree on those graphs through specified linear maps.

backbone: Positive point-descendant lower bounds give an algebraically independent joint eigenvalue tuple of quantum divisor operators, yielding rho independent curve degrees; the ordered-chain method then gives the inequality and equality case.
quote: Our argument first detects independent curve degrees in quantum correspondences. Proper covering families enter only at equality, when all the selected degrees are minimal.

backbone: Build relaxed [-1,1] coefficients from a balanced torus polynomial sampled along quadratic waves packed by hypergraph matchings, then round to signs by discrepancy with small Fourier error.
quote: The construction makes the normalized Fourier maximum close to one while keeping $N^{-1}\sum_k X_{N,k}^2$ close to one. The latter condition makes $\mu(X_N)/N$ small.

backbone: An affinely normalized variational representation of support functionals plus a spherical-harmonic sign estimate gives a strict norm inequality and bilinear inequality implying Petty's bound with equality cases.
quote: Our proof uses the classical first-variation and spherical-transform frameworks, but requires estimates and an affine normalization that apply to arbitrary bodies.

backbone: Subdivide Bang's two-cylinder covering of the regular tetrahedron into narrow angular sectors with tilted axes, verify coverage, and expand the total base area to show a strict quadratic saving.
quote: We construct a counterexample with compact triangular bases.

backbone: Define an explicit polynomial-time language whose slices, with probabilistically chosen parameter bits, have tiny correlation with bounded-width CNFs under random restrictions; summing over middle gates contradicts positive acceptance density.
quote: We construct a language with a data block and parameter blocks. Membership evaluates a polynomial at a linear hash of the data, in the quotient ring specified by another input block.

backbone: Prepare LP openings on a constant grid, apply tapered iterative rounding analysed by a potential and finite drift inequality, derandomize by moment-matching distributions, then remove the additive surplus via Li-Svensson.
quote: The proof separates the preparation of fractional openings, their iterative rounding, and the removal of randomness and surplus.

backbone: Construct a simulator: split the tape into blocks and epochs, write the outcome as factored word recurrences, and evaluate them with a shared Cook-Mertz register pool in T^{2/5} space.
quote: Its procedure adds a scalar multiple of a word's fixed augmented value to one chosen register and restores every other register, from arbitrary contents on entry.

backbone: Build by induction a finite minimum of affine functions whose active slopes approximate exponent vectors; its compact convex plateau is forward invariant and absorbing since the minimum increases elsewhere.
quote: The proof will use a finite minimum of affine functions on the positive orthant. Its essential property is that an active slope approximates the exponent vector of the point where it is active.

backbone: Take an explicit 13-point 22-triple incidence graph; build a rank-layer finite-field matrix kernel whose sign-parity correlation gives a negative density term, symmetrize, and sample a finite host graph.
quote: We disprove Sidorenko's conjecture with a bipartite graph on 35 vertices and 66 edges: its homomorphism density in some finite simple graph is smaller than the conjectured lower bound.

backbone: Extract a large low-resistance tree packing via hierarchy shortcuts and a fixed-point limit, then iterate an interlacing-based sparsification preserving packings until a thin spanning tree remains.
quote: Section~\ref{sec:iteration} combines the two representations, iterates the sparsification, and proves the binary-multiplicity reduction.

backbone: Influence controls high Fourier degrees; low-degree mass is bounded via random vertex-block restrictions and biased hypercontractivity; Russo's formula turns the variance-influence bound into threshold width.
quote: Its squared nonconstant coefficients sum to the variance; weighting them by $|S|$ gives $\sigma^2I_p(f)$. Thus the influence controls high degrees. The task is to bound the remaining mass using symmetry.

backbone: From an Abels-type group build a selection functor with unbounded extinction, realize it by a bimodule complex simulated by an ordinary bimodule X, and take A = D ⋉ X.
quote: We construct a finite-dimensional complex algebra whose finite-dimensional modules have unbounded finite projective dimensions.

backbone: Reduce to six-part Schur multiplicities; cover them by canonical-map stabilization for b>=30, first-row and shift certificates, recurrences, and program-verified certificates for remaining degrees and a tail band.
quote: The present certificates combine such calculations with bounds on entire families of multiplicities, leaving only a small band for exact comparison.

backbone: Matching bounds: an enriched Hamilton-Jacobi contact-point comparison gives the upper bound; a cavity computation with cascades and cited path-concavity gives the lower bound; smoothness is then removed.
quote: The upper bound is Proposition~\ref{upper:bound}, and Proposition~\ref{cav:lower-bound} gives the matching lower bound.

backbone: Matching bounds: perturbed upper comparison via Haar-rotation overlap identities and ultrametricity, and a cavity lower bound whose maximizing field uses concavity of the Ising field functional.
quote: The lower bound will identify a field whose conditional two-spin products equal the overlap quantile. To turn that identity into the supremum defining $S$, we need concavity of $\ell$ in its covariance levels.

backbone: Reduce via Bonk-Kleiner to bounded combinatorial modulus; assuming unbounded modulus, a limiting scalar function and measure yield a contradiction in the exponential-record and subexponential (probability flow) cases.
quote: Assume this fails. Record indices permit comparison of $M(N-l)$ with $M(N)$, and lead to two growth cases.

backbone: Induct along the Magnus hierarchy; each step's combination theorem needs annular flaring, proved by contradiction: nonflaring annuli give a stationary current whose carriers have zero mass.
quote: The Freiheitssatz makes an inductive approach possible: a Magnus splitting has a smaller one-relator vertex group and free edge groups.

backbone: Mass-deform the supercharge and compute its index p(N); in the massless limit, proper-cluster null profiles account for p(N)-1 dimensions by simultaneous induction on N, leaving one state.
quote: Closing the simultaneous induction

backbone: Null-cut Ward identities and a two-horizon modular spectral comparison show the residual dilation charge vanishes, yielding a dimension-two scalar L with virial divergence box L and a traceless improvement.
quote: Under these hypotheses, the stress tensor admits a symmetric, conserved, traceless improvement with unchanged translation and Lorentz charges.

backbone: Construct a C*-algebra of shifts on vector bundles with expanding, normalized bundle maps; Chern classes exclude proper infiniteness while expansion forces a uniform quasitrace additivity defect.
quote: We construct such an algebra and obtain a fixed positive pair witnessing nonadditivity.

backbone: Assume a cosmetic pair, reduced to genus two and slopes ±2; a nonzero instanton count and a nonabelian-monopole cobordism count forcing it to vanish give a contradiction.
quote: If a smooth nontrivial knot $K\subset S^3$ has distinct purely cosmetic slopes, then $g(K)=2$ and the two slopes are $-2$ and $2$.

backbone: Construct an explicit ordered fracture filtration of the height-three overlap, identify its attachments via cohomology of completed Lubin-Tate strata, and show one is nonzero, refuting strong splitting.
quote: For every prime \(p\geq5\), we construct an explicit eight-stage filtration of \(L_2L_{K(3)}\mathbb S_p^\wedge\) by the local-sphere layers in the height-three chromatic-splitting pattern.

backbone: Construct bounded uniformly discrete blocks from colored random-regular-like graphs attached to finitely many label anchors; any norm-p finite-rank near-identity yields signed measures contradicted by incidence-averaged scalar tests; wedge the blocks.
quote: We construct a countable uniformly discrete metric space whose real Lipschitz-free space has the approximation property but fails the bounded approximation property, answering Kalton's question negatively.

backbone: If no compatible form exists, separation gives a positive current vanishing on closed invariant forms; mass-growth, regularization and density estimates make it contradict the taming form.
quote: In the argument below, separation gives a positive functional vanishing on closed invariant forms. An explicit elliptic lift and quantitative current estimates connect this obstruction to the existence of a taming form.

backbone: Reduce to the two transition volumes; nonstandard minimizers fall into three- or four-vertex patterns, each excluded by planar-section identities, nesting estimates and certified scalar inequalities.
quote: If every minimizer at \(V_1\) and \(V_2\) is standard, then \(I=F\) on \([0,1]\), and every minimizer is one of the standard regions of Lemma~\ref{pre:standard}.

backbone: Reduce to rectifiable minimizers, take blow-up limits, exclude isolated bounded crack components by an energy-comparison contradiction, then classify limits and apply known regularity.
quote: In the generalized-limit formulation recalled below, these classification results leave the possible bounded components of a limiting crack as the remaining obstruction.
